analyticalQuestion: Does finite Galerkin evolution corroborate the positive-time internal target-shell zero from the local NSE flow-map construction, and does double scaling separate its entry atom from the bare normalized Leray time budget?
takeaway: The shot target shell crosses zero at a positive internal time, the precompensation approaches its first-order coefficient, the entry atom agrees with the scale-zero slope charge, and the leading atom-to-bare-budget ratio grows like lambda squared.
nonColorEncoding: solid, dashed, dash-dot, and dotted lines
filled and open circle, square, and diamond markers
direct left and right axis labels

panels.A: precompensation norm ratio over five tau values plus one refined independent point
panels.B: signed principal target coefficient and transverse shell residual across the internal event
panels.C: entry atom, slope-charge reconstruction, seed limit, and one refined independent point
panels.D: exact leading atom, bare budget, and ratio under double scaling

claimBoundary: Panels A-C are finite Fourier-Galerkin corroboration in the x3-independent three-component invariant sector. Panel D is an exact leading asymptotic ledger. No continuum Galerkin error estimate, DNS claim, Leray occupation bound, repeated-entry packing, singularity, continuation, or regularity theorem is shown.
